title: Realizing what "Polish" means
author: fapfap_ahh
selftext:
As I develop my game, what I considered "polished" was far from what it really meant to playtesters of the demo. Game concept was fun but the world felt empty, unalive, and unatmospheric. Like someone cobbled a bunch of random forest objects together.

I took a step back and did research to compare how my current game world would compare to other indie games of the same genre. This helped me realize just how much was missing from my own game.

My last few working sessions have been mainly focused on redefining what polish means and happily, we're getting there! The video hopefully shows much improvement from what you've seen on my YouTube/itchio.

Here's all the I've done the last few sessions:

* Added multiple different vegetation plants and shrubs (24 variations)
* Different types of dead branches (4 variations)
* Proper snow accumulation on snow and world items.
* Ground reflections and sun glare
* Bloom where it's appropriate
* VFX Graph for much better window/snow/weather effects
* New more realistic clouds
* Snow updrifts and breezes
* Up to 12 ground textures blended by height. Sun sparkle on snow, fresh/trampled/thin snow, forest litter, packed snow, yard snow, ice, darker ground at trunk bases.
* Sun glare
* winter color grade
* Much much more tree density (+ proper sizing/scattering)
* Trails, dense patches of trees, open areas
* Elevation depth changes for proper "outside forest" feel
* Redone the camera movement for the handheld tool / weapon
   * Diagonal arc
   * hit stop on impact
   * camera shake on tool/weapon use
   * camera zoom/blur on sprint
* Redone camera "view" depending on weather (sun glare, snow blindness)
* Changed all IMGUI to UGUI.
* Reworked menu and settings buttons/text/sounds/animations
* More readable font across the board
* Resized HUD/Alerts/Minimap
* Added more detail to Minimap

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Hey friend! Good questions!

I use Unity alongside my own "AI GameKit" I've built. This includes my dev console, AI automations, pipeline scripts for any and all assets (import/edit/decimate/animate/trim), AI GPU rendering/playtesting, CPU/GPU profiling, amongst other things.

Essentially the GameKit handles all the "engine logic" while the game itself is just "what asset to use, where it goes, and how to present it."

Attached are example images that show a snippet of this, it was part of a presentation I did at my job to show what I was doing outside of work.

replies.author: OkVariety8064
replies.body:
Do I understand it correctly that your workflow is such that you have built some sort of "scaffold project" with an FPS template and a set of asset packs, and then you ask Claude to add those features you mentioned (like snow updrifts and breezes) one at a time, and then you evaluate how the whole thing looks in that sort of iterative loop?

In any case, the end result looks excellent, and has a strong feel of being a real place. I was wondering how the ferns stay green, but apparently there are evergreen varieties. Or perhaps the winter has just arrived. In any case, the fact that such thoughts come from watching this shows it's already doing a lot to give the impression of a real biome.

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Pretty much? 

The scaffold is not an openable Unity project and it's not FPS specific. However, it does have MD files that instruct Claude (and the user) on how to build a game with it, starting with a new project in Unity.

The scaffold itself is all the C# scripts that can be used as interfaces & components as soon as you start, but, on their own you won't get anything out of them but a blank skybox.

This basically means you can say "hey let's start a game with this gamekit, here is my concept, here are some assets, I want to play it this way." 

It'll get you to an early playable dev build from which you can start to tune and add upon.

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Any asset I need whether it's from blender or another source, 3d or audio or texture, I have an automated pipeline for it.

I can take a model and it's pieces to animate it how I want. I can also trim/edit/manipulate audio and give it spatial awareness.

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Anything "repeatable" don't have Claude do over and over, tell it to make it a script that can be reused with inputs and save that somewhere, then reference via [Claude.MD](http://Claude.MD) AND Claude Memory. I've pasted the prompt I got started with to make my "animator script pipeline" so feel free to use it for your benefit :)

\-------

Here is the prompt for the "3d model animator from it's parts":

  
I'm making a first-person Unity (URP) game. I have free Asset Store gun models with no

animations, just separately named child meshes (e.g. "Slider", "Hammer", "Trigger",

"Magazine"). Write a MonoBehaviour GunAnimator that animates them entirely from code:



\- A serializable GunRigSpec: child names for slide / hammer / trigger / magazine (any can be

  empty), slide travel (m), hammer angle (deg), trigger travel (m) or angle (deg), kick back

  (m), muzzle climb (deg), mag travel (m), reload tilt, and "slide locks open when empty".

\- Attach(gun, spec) at equip; find parts by name recursively; remember their rest poses.

\- Barrel axis: the gun's long axis already points along the hand's forward, so convert the

  hand's forward/up into the gun's local space once and use those as barrel/up/lateral axes.

\- For hammer and trigger, decide the rotation sign by rotating the part's mesh centre +10 deg

  about the lateral axis and checking whether it moved toward the rear.

\- Small static curve functions of "seconds since shot" / "reload progress 0..1": kick,

  slide cycle, trigger squeeze, reload tilt, mag out, mag back in.

\- Public hooks: OnFired(), OnDryFire(), BeginReload(seconds). In LateUpdate apply everything

  as LOCAL offsets on top of the base pose (never overwrite the holding code's pose).

\- Reload: at \~35% clone the magazine, give it a BoxCollider from its renderer bounds and a

  Rigidbody with a small downward push, destroy it after 3 s; hide the real mag briefly,

  then slide it back in.

\- Camera recoil: expose an "aiming 0..1" value and a CameraShake01 setting; kick the camera's

  local rotation up (plus small random yaw/roll per shot), smaller on the sights.

\- Restore all rest poses (and the camera rotation) on disable/destroy.

\- A MuzzleWorld property: the front end of the model's bounds along the barrel axis.

No animation clips, no Animator. Keep it one file plus the spec class.

comments.author: pickleunicorn

Well, there are some things that are weird to me because you're merging hyper realistic world with anime animations. Mainly :
- the colours on the water
- the visible wind 
- and yet the snow is falling straight to the ground 

To me you should rework you're water, and your wind. Don't make it visible but add it some weight. The wind should act onto the water, the snow, the branches, the trees, the ground, ...

comments.author: orellanaed
comments.body: What makes a forest read as cobbled together is usually every prop standing alone on flat terrain, so grouping them in clusters of one big piece with a few small ones around it and adding ground clutter and some fog for depth will do more than any new asset.

comments.author: Tripone
comments.body:
Polish might not be the thing to aim for when playtesters give that kind of feedback. Think hard if polishing is the phase you are really in.

I watched the gameplay demo and it seems to overwhelm with systems and text. If you would slice everything away but the core, what would the 30 second loop be like?

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Check radar, check radio, check transponder, use binos outside, evaluate threat, ignore or escalate. Convince superior to launch missile if escalating.

Side items would be hunting, fishing, maintaining / repairing equipment, exploring side quests.

The alerts do seem overwhelming! I'll take a sweep of them to see which ones can be reduced or moved to other systems
